agency.name: North Carolina Department of Health and Human Services — Division of Mental Health, Developmental Disabilities and Substance Use Services (DMH/DD/SUS)

narrAffiliate.name: North Carolina Association of Recovery Residences (NCARR)

narrNote: NCARR is on NARR's official affiliate list (narronline.org/affiliates, fetched in-run 2026-10-22); its own site was fetched and verified. The organization's own name is 'Association' — some secondary sources incorrectly say 'Alliance'.
notes: Agency is NC's SAMHSA Single State Agency for substance use (the DMH/DD/SUS division within NCDHHS, per SAMHSA/NASADAD SSA listings); division landing page fetched and verified. Agency phone is the NCDHHS Customer Service Center number published on the official NCDHHS Hotlines page. NC delivers public behavioral health regionally through LME/MCOs (Tailored Plans): NCDHHS publishes an LME/MCO directory, but that page's fetch was blocked by research-tool rate limiting on 2026-10-22, so countyDirectory is null rather than linked unverified — use the verified division page as the entry point. NC has no separate SUD-specific statewide crisis line (acute crisis routes via 988 and LME/MCO crisis lines); the state-published statewide line is the NC Peer Warmline, operated by Promise Resource Network under NCDHHS contract, listed as stateCrisis. NC Medicaid publishes stand-alone SUD clinical coverage policies (SAIOP, SACOT, residential levels of care) under the verified Medicaid hub.
